title: Natural Developing Moves | Scandinavian Defense: Modern | GM Naroditsky’s Top Theory Speedrun

moves.spoken: The bishop check on b5 — an easy-to-learn, effective line against the Nf6 Scandinavian. It forces Black to block and commit awkwardly.
moves.teaches: The b5 check is a low-theory way to get a pleasant, slightly better game against the Scandinavian.
moves.plans: Provoke a clumsy block, then develop with a pull.

moves.spoken: Most players block with the bishop to d7 — but that piece is poorly placed: it deprives the queen's knight of its natural d7-square and clogs Black's development.
moves.teaches: A blocking bishop on d7 is a liability — it robs the b8-knight of its best square.
moves.plans: Keep that bishop stuck; don't trade it off.

moves.spoken: Retreat the bishop to e2 rather than allowing an exchange — the whole idea is to leave Black's awkward d7-bishop on the board, a lasting inconvenience.
moves.teaches: Preserve the opponent's bad piece by declining the trade.
moves.plans: Recover the d5-pawn and take the centre.

moves.spoken: Grab the centre with the pawn to d4 — and it is important to start with d4, not a sloppy e6-type move that would leave the bishop and the g2-square under fire.
moves.teaches: Move order matters — take the centre with d4 before the pieces can be harassed.

moves.spoken: Develop the knight to c6 — principled, by-the-book play. With the extra space and Black's awkward bishop, White simply stands more comfortably.
moves.teaches: When you have a structural edge, keep developing soundly — the advantage compounds.
moves.plans: Finish development and press the space.
